newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end with big loss but off lows.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end with big loss but off lows.

text.p: French shares closed sharply lower on Thursday after being swamped by losses in the late afternoon, although the blue-chip CAC-40 index did partially recoup the declines.

Traders said comments by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan fuelled fears of a preemptive rise in interest rates at next Tuesday's Fed policy meeting, plunging the CAC to a session low of 2,541.49 before steadying.
The index closed the monthly account down 43.05 points or 1.66 percent at 2,553.72. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 28 at 2,555 from Wednesday's close.
"The market is falling because of the declarations of Alan Greenspan," said a broker. "Many people fear there will be a possible increase in interest rates."

He added that there was a great deal of uncertainty in the markets and stock prices were either very high or very low. Every sentence uttered by Greenspan was seized on an indicator for interest rate intentions.
Interest rate nerves were driving prices lower despite the "good" company results reported.
Another broker said investors were looking at a buying zone on the CAC index at around 2,530-2,550.

Credit Lyonnais ended down 1.81 percent at 190. The bank posted a 1996 net attributable profit of 202 million francs, in line with market estimates, which included restructuring charges of 2.48 billion francs and 200 million for moving to European monetary union in 1999.

Renault closed flat at 138 francs. The carmaker reported a net attributable loss of 5.25 billion francs, the first in a decade. That includes a 3.91 billion franc charge for closing the Belgian Vilvoorde plant and job losses in France. It passed the 1996 dividend.

The luxury goods group gave back the strong gains posted in the day on the back of a bullish presentation by chairman Bernaud Arnault. Non-domestic brokers tended to take a more sceptical view of the stock, pointing at worries over its strategy with DFS and where growth would come from.
Canal Plus ended 4.78 percent higher at 1,118, as analysts welcomed chairman Pierre Lescure's hopes of a successful settlement to disputes in Germany and Spain.
Among rare risers was Lagardere, rebounding from weakness seen since the government's relaunch of the Thomson-CSF
